description: Phase 14 certified the year-end settlement of a provider-switch year. Phase 15 certifies what the engine does in the CALCULATED cutoffs of such a year: the withholding on each payslip, whether the run is held for review, and that the settlement then closes the year exactly (tax due minus everything withheld).

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (taxable compensation to 10,417 exempt; to 16,667 at 15% over 10,417; to 33,333 at 937.50 + 20% over 16,667) and the annual table (to 400,000 at 15% over 250,000).
sources.deMinimis: BIR RR 29-2025 de minimis ceilings (repository DE_MINIMIS_2026 table): uniform and clothing allowance 8,000 a year.
sources.thirteenthMonthAndBenefits: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e): 13th-month pay and other benefits share one exemption of 90,000.
sources.sss: SSS 2025 schedule: employee share 5% of the monthly salary credit, credit capped at 35,000 (1,750 a month, 875 a cutoff); 30,000 gives 1,500 a month (750 a cutoff).

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing. Provider switch on 2026-07-01: January-June are six imported monthly rows per worker (basic 30,000, SSS 1,500, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 200, withholding 1,007.40); July-December are cutoffs 13-24 calculated by the engine. Basic is 30,000 a month.

Calculated-cutoff withholding is on taxable compensation = gross - SSS - PhilHealth - Pag-IBIG with no exempt other-benefit excess: for gross 18,000 (basic 15,000 + de minimis 3,000): 15,000 - 875 - 375 - 100 = 13,650, tax 0.15 x (13,650 - 10,417) = 484.95. Without a grant: 15,000 - 750 - 375 - 100 = 13,775, tax 0.15 x 3,358 = 503.70. De minimis (inside its ceiling) and other-benefit excess inside the 90,000 pool are not taxable compensation.
Total withheld = imported 6 x 1,007.40 = 6,044.40 plus 12 calculated cutoffs. The settlement's adjustment is tax due minus total withheld.
The 13th month is the accrued basic, 30,000, and joins the 90,000 pool in the settlement. Year-end reads Released runs, so each calculated run is set to Released in the fixture.

poolExhaustedBeforeYearEnd.description: Uniform allowance: previous provider 6,000 a month; engine grant 15,000 a month (7,500 a cutoff). Union paid 126,000: exempt 8,000, excess 118,000; with the 13th month 148,000 against the 90,000 pool. The previous provider's rows carry a category breakdown, so the engine counts the 28,000 already in the pool: its room is used up after 8 engine cutoffs (28,000 + 8 x 7,500 = 88,000), cutoff 21 has overflow 5,500 (taxable 19,150, tax 937.50 + 0.20 x 2,483 = 1,434.10) and cutoffs 22-24 overflow 7,500 (taxable 21,150, tax 937.50 + 0.20 x 4,483 = 1,834.10). Withheld 6,044.40 + 8 x 484.95 + 1,434.10 + 3 x 1,834.10 = 16,860.40; collect 20,565.00 - 16,860.40 = 3,704.60. Current-cutoff tax includes the verified imported de minimis and 13th-month minimum, but prior other 90,000-pool benefits are not separately captured by the import schema; the review hold remains until complete YTD evidence is reconciled.

ceilingExhaustedByBothSources.description: Phase 14 inputs: uniform allowance 6,000 a month from each source. Union 72,000: exempt 8,000, excess 64,000, pool 94,000 (4,000 over). Verified breakdown: the engine's 36,000 is all pool excess (previous 28,000 + 36,000 = 64,000, under 90,000), so nothing is taxable inside the cutoffs; the 13th month in the settlement takes the pool to 94,000. Current-cutoff tax includes the verified imported de minimis and 13th-month minimum, but prior other 90,000-pool benefits are not separately captured by the import schema; the review hold remains until complete YTD evidence is reconciled.

historyWithoutDeMinimis.description: Phase 14 inputs: previous provider paid no de minimis; engine grant 6,000 a month. Exempt 8,000, excess 28,000.

controlNoGrant.description: Control: imported history but no de minimis grant at all. Nothing to hold: Ready, no flags, withholding 503.70 a cutoff, and the settlement balances to a 1.20 collection.

limitations: Only the engine's behavior in the calculated cutoffs of a provider-switch year with one de minimis category is certified; the release approval workflow and the HTTP/role gates are not exercised.
SSS is computed by the engine on gross including de minimis, as in Phase 14.

A worker whose imported rows lack a readable category breakdown (case historyWithoutDeMinimis) keeps the review hold and the unadjusted withholding: nothing is assumed about what the previous provider paid.

A complete previous-provider 90,000-pool figure is not recorded in historical_payroll_entries; reported de minimis/13th-month consumption improves withholding but cannot authorize payroll release. Even workers with category breakdowns remain in Exception for independent pool reconciliation.
